description: Configuration for the automated data-update pipeline. Add new keywords or feeds here (not by editing breaches.json/companies.json directly) to expand what the pipeline looks for.

regulatory_breach_registers.description: Official government breach-notification registers that publish structured or searchable lists of reported breaches. These generally do not offer RSS feeds, so the pipeline scrapes or periodically diffs their published lists/CSVs rather than polling them like RSS. Included here for future automation development.

sources.name: California AG Data Security Breach List
sources.notes: Publishes a searchable list and downloadable CSV of breach notices affecting 500+ California residents.

sources.name: Washington State AG Data Breach Notifications
sources.notes: Interactive directory of all breach notices submitted since 2015.

sources.name: Maine AG Data Security Breaches
sources.notes: State breach reporting service and historical archive.

sources.name: Texas AG Data Security Breach Reports
sources.notes: Searchable public register of breach reports affecting Texas residents.

sources.name: UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
sources.notes: UK GDPR/PECR breach reporting authority; does not publish a full public register but issues enforcement notices and guidance.

sources.name: Privacy Rights Clearinghouse Data Breach Chronology
sources.notes: Aggregates 75,000+ reported breaches since 2005 from 15 US government agency sources into one searchable database.

sources.name: Identity Theft Resource Center (ITRC) Breach Alert
sources.notes: Comprehensive US breach database since 2005; subscription required for full alerting, but summary reports are public.

hibp_integration.notes: If a HIBP_API_KEY secret is configured, the workflow queries the HIBP 'latest breaches' endpoint (https://haveibeenpwned.com/api/v3/breaches) and filters DataClasses for identity-document-related fields (e.g. 'Passport numbers', 'Government issued IDs', 'Driver's license numbers'). Without a key, this step is skipped and the workflow relies solely on RSS/keyword matching.

supplementary_breach_apis.description: Additional free/low-friction breach-metadata APIs that could be integrated into future pipeline versions to broaden discovery beyond RSS. None require payment for basic breach-source lookups as of research date.

sources.name: LeakCheck Public API
sources.notes: Free, unauthenticated API returning breach source names and exposed data categories (never raw leaked data) for a queried identifier.

sources.name: Recent Breaches API
sources.notes: Free, CORS-enabled JSON API and RSS feed (https://recentbreaches.com/feed.xml) of the latest ~50 published breaches, no signup required for non-commercial use.

sources.name: 9Ghz Data Breach Monitor Open API
sources.notes: REST API for breach list and per-account breach queries; used only for keyword/company-name discovery, never for querying real user identifiers.

review_policy: All candidate entries discovered by the pipeline are written to data/pending-review.json and opened as a pull request/issue for manual approval before being merged into breaches.json or companies.json. This prevents unverified rumors from being published as confirmed breaches.
